The Vupp engine, in full

Every call an app can make on the Vupp handheld, generated from the firmware source (firmware/vupp/components/apprt/vupp_apprt_api.c) at engine v17. If a call is on this site it exists on the device; if it is not, it does not.

Before the API

An app is Lua 5.4 files plus an app.json. The device runs one app at a time in a fresh VM, calls vupp.init() once and then vupp.update(dt) and vupp.draw(gfx) every frame. Colors are palette indices, never hex. The canvas is 480×320 with "hires": true in the manifest, and every coordinate is in that space.

This site is the complete surface, but it is not the place to start. The SDK page and vupp docs teach the subset a first app should use, and why. Come here when you need to know exactly what an argument does.

The API, by what it does

Shapes and text7 calls. The whole no-assets surface. Every app can call these, and many of the best ones in the library call nothing else.
Sprites and images6 calls. Needs art files in the app package. Each one is a silent no-op when the app ships none.
Heightfield terrain4 calls. The Comanche-style voxel-ish renderer (engine v4-v6): Lua drives the camera, C marches the columns.
Meshes6 calls. The whole-model fast path (engine v11+). One call draws a model: transform, cull, light and rasterise all happen in C.
Block worlds13 calls. The voxel engine (engine v17). A byte-per-cell grid in PSRAM, remeshed per chunk and rasterised in one call.
Input3 calls. Read the pad every frame; there is no event queue.
Sound3 calls. A six-voice mixer. Only vupp.tone needs no files, and it is enough: a blip on every input is most of what makes a game feel alive.
Saving and data9 calls. The app's persisted, parent-visible state (docs/11-app-contract.md).
Everything else6 calls. Time, randomness, module loading, and leaving the app.

Lifecycle

Define these as globals on the pre-existing vupp table. None of them are calls you make.

vupp.init

function vupp.init()

Once, before the first frame.

vupp.update

function vupp.update(dt)

Every frame. dt is seconds since the last one, so multiply movement by it.

vupp.draw

function vupp.draw(gfx)

Every frame; draws the whole screen. The gfx table it receives is permanent, so an app may keep a reference to it and call gfx.theight from update.

vupp.on_exit

function vupp.on_exit()

Optional. Runs on every teardown (pause-menu exit, restart, parent command, quiet hours) before the store is flushed.

Reading the flags

Three things stop a call from working even though it exists. Each is marked on the call:

capability: touch needs asset files stub

  • capability: the call is not injected at all unless app.json lists it in "capabilities". Calling it without that is a nil-index crash.
  • needs asset files: it reads a file from the app package. With no such file it is a silent no-op or returns false; it never raises. This is the trap, because the app runs and nothing appears.
  • stub: registered so calling it is safe, but it does nothing yet.

vupp.store.getKey was never written.
vupp.store.setValue is nil | bool | number | string | small table.

The sandbox

The VM opens only base, math, string, table, utf8. There is no io, os, package, debug or coroutine. They are never opened, so they are nil rather than restricted. These base functions are removed as well: 

dofile, loadfile, load, collectgarbage

So require "x" is vupp.import("x"), os.time() is vupp.time() (or vupp.date() for a wall clock), and there is no way to reach the filesystem except the asset-loading calls above. print exists and goes to the device log.
